sections.name: MedicalNERExtractor
sections.title: Entity finder by document type
sections.what: Searches OCR text for lab result patterns for five tests, and for four medicine names in prescriptions. Each match becomes an entity entry, and the total is logged. Discharge summaries return nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: a rule-based first version that needs no trained model. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: Test names and medicines not on the lists are silently dropped, so missing results give no warning.

summary: Finds medical facts in raw OCR text with simple text patterns: lab results for five named tests and medicine names from a short fixed list.
purpose: Pulls out test names, values, and units, or medicine names, so later steps can structure them.
why: Likely reason: a simple first version. The file calls the patterns simple and the medicine list a stub. Reason for the mention of SpaCy in the description is not stated.
how: For lab reports, it searches the text for five named tests followed by a number and a unit, and records each match with its parts. For prescriptions, it checks whether any of four medicine names appears in the text. It logs the count and returns the list.
inputs: Raw text from the OCR step and the document type.
outputs: A list of found entries, each with a label, the matched text, and details such as the parameter, value, and unit.
risks: Only five lab tests and four medicines are recognized, so other results are silently missed. The file description mentions SpaCy, but no SpaCy code appears here. Lab matches are not checked against ranges in this file. Matching ignores case and also matches inside longer words.
debug: If a test is missing from the results, check the OCR text and whether the name and spacing match the pattern. For prescriptions, check that the medicine is in the fixed list. The logs show how many entries were found.
